articles.title: How Dolly Parton told her life story through six iconic songs
articles.summary: A legendary singer-songwriter, her music covered themes around love, loss, female empowerment and spirituality.
articles.body:
The much-loved US singer-songwriter, actress and philanthropist Dolly Parton, who has died aged 80 , was known as the Queen of Country.

Raised in Tennessee, she rose to fame in the late 1960s with hits that bridged country and pop music.

Her songs covered deeply personal themes around growing up poor, love and loss, as well as female empowerment and spirituality.

Live updates: Dolly Parton, legendary US country singer, dies aged 80

Dolly Parton: The country legend who sang from the heart

Following Parton's death, here is a look back at her life through the lens of six iconic songs.

Let's start with Dolly Parton's own personal favourite, her 1971 acoustic country-folk ditty, Coat of Many Colors , external .

The autobiographical track, taken from the album of the same name, tells the heart-stirring tale of how she grew up poor - as one of 12 siblings - but rich in love.

In her book, Songteller: My Life in Lyrics, Parton described it as a "little story" that covers "a world of things", with teachings about bullying, acceptance, love and good parenting.

The lyrics go: " Now I know we had no money, but I was rich as I could be / In my coat of many colors my momma made for me " .

The song has been covered by the likes of Shania Twain and Eva Cassidy, and Rolling Stone magazine put it in second place in its list of Parton's top 50 songs , external .

"Had it been the only song she'd ever written, the expression of overwhelming pride and crushing anguish... would have secured her indelible legacy," the US magazine wrote in 2023.

Coat of Many Colors is also the title of Parton's own children's book, and a 2015 TV movie based on her life - starring Alyvia Alyn Lind as the precocious young singer dreaming of fame.

Her mother, Avie Lee Parton, even made her daughter a new patchwork coat to put on display at the museum inside the Dollywood theme park in her home state of Tennessee.

Parton penned many songs about all different aspects of her relationship with her devoted husband Carl Dean , who ran an asphalt paving business in Nashville.

This included the fear that she might lose him, specifically to a red-headed bank clerk who had flirted with him early on in their marriage.

We all know her by now, of course, as the infamous Jolene , external .

With its fast fingerstyle minor riff, the song was nominated for a Grammy in 1974 and gave Parton her second number one single on the Billboard Hot Country Singles chart and her first foray into the main Hot 100 chart (60).

It also showed Parton at her most vulnerable, making it all the more relatable.

Instead of shedding tears or vowing revenge, we hear the protagonist in the song begging the mistress who holds the power to relinquish it.

"She got this terrible crush on my husband," Parton told US media in 2008. "And he just loved going to the bank because she paid him so much attention. It was kinda like a running joke between us - I was saying, 'Hell, you're spending a lot of time at the bank. I don't believe we've got that kind of money.'"

Parton had met Dean outside a laundromat on the first day she arrived in Nashville as an 18-year-old aspiring singer. The pair were married for 60 years, until his death in 2025 .

A notoriously private man, he was "a little embarrassed" when she wrote Jolene, Parton said in a 2023 interview with BBC's The One Show , external , adding that "actually, it wasn't as serious [as it sounds]. I was just jealous 'cause she was a beautiful woman and he was just flirting.

"So it gave me a great idea for a song. There's always a Jolene in somebody's life."

She joked that later in life when she saw her, by now, much older husband snoozing in his chair at home, she thought Jolene "can have him now... where's Jolene when you need her?!"

Jolene is her most popular song, having been streamed more than 913 million times on Spotify. Critics from Rolling Stone to the Guardian , external agree it's her best.

Beyoncé gave it a modern rewrite for her 2024 Cowboy Carter , external album, changing the lyrics from: " I'm begging of you, please, don't take my man " to " I'm warning you, don't come for my man. "

Despite the romantic sounding title, this 1974 song , external is actually the sound of Parton tenderly asking her musical mentor, Porter Wagoner, to let her go and pursue her solo career.

Parton was 21 when she joined Wagoner's variety TV show. They released a string of duets and toured together, leading fans to think they were an item.

But they had a complicated relationship, with Parton later writing in another book, Star of the Show: My Life on Stage, that she felt Wagoner saw her rise as a "threat".

"I was making my way as an artist, and he was already an established one. It was his show, but I was trying to grow in the business and grow as an artist myself."

On the track we hear her sing: " Bittersweet memories / That is all I'm taking with me".

Rough Trade's music blog , external once described it as being "heartwarming in its sentiment, crushing in its delivery."

Elvis Presley was set to record a cover of the song in 1974, but Parton made the difficult decision to back out of the deal when his manager demanded half of the songwriting rights.

"I said, 'I can't do that'," she told Howard Stern in 2023. "Of course I cried all night about that."

Parton re-recorded I Will Always Love You in 1982 for her starring role in the musical comedy film, The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas.

But arguably the most iconic version comes courtesy of Whitney Houston who can be heard booming it out in another film, 1992's The Bodyguard. Her version remains the biggest-selling US single by a female artist.

Parton said she heard the power ballad version for the first time on the radio, and felt so overwhelmed that she had to pull over to avoid crashing her Cadillac.

Whitney Houston took her "little country song" and made it "so much more", she said.

With Parton's newfound professional freedom came a renewed sense of hope, optimism and spirituality - as heard on her 1977 track, Light of a Clean Blue Morning.

She recalled leaving Wagoner's office after their musical split and driving home in a rainstorm, until the clouds parted, giving way to sunlight and an idea for another new song.

Parton - whose earliest performances were in church as a child - referred to it as her "song of deliverance", helping her on the road to stardom.

The lyrics were reworked for the soundtrack to her 1992 romantic comedy film, Straight Talk.

And in early 2026 she released a new charity version of the song , external , in aid of pediatric cancer research, featuring her goddaughter Miley Cyrus, Lainey Wilson, Queen Latifah and Reba.

This defiant anthem of female empowerment, released in 1980, was the most transformative of her career.

Already well established as a singer, 9 To 5 , external brought Parton over into the mainstream popular culture.

She wrote the country-tinged southern soul number as the theme tune for the comedy film of the same name, which saw her make her movie debut alongside Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin.

It tells the story of three working women who live out their fantasies of getting even with, and overthrowing, their company's bigot of a boss (played by Dabney Coleman).

The song's distinctive tapping beat at the start is none other than her acrylic nails: "I always play the nails and I'd come up with little things that I would see on the set, like 'I tumble out of bed and I stumble to the kitchen'… And I thought, 'Wow, that sounds like a typewriter,'" she once explained.

Parton won two Grammys for the chart-topping tune, which was also nominated for an Oscar, and later spawned a Broadway musical and a documentary.

A modern day karaoke classic, Parton recorded this hit with fellow US country star Kenny Rogers , external as the lead single for his 1983 album, Eyes That See in the Dark.

The deep love song sold millions of copies and topped both the country and pop charts at the same time.

It was actually written for them by the Bee Gees, intended as a Motown-inspired duet. The Gibb brothers later recorded their own version and performed it live.

Parton and Rogers' rendition, though, remains one of most popular country-pop duets of all time and a classic of the genre.

Their collaboration was "another thing I'm as proud of as anything I ever did in my musical career," she told Smooth Radio , external 40 years on, in 2023.

She added: "You want to do well and keeping up with the likes of Barry [Gibb] and Kenny [Rogers], but I just figure I'll just always be me and do me and that seems to work."

Down from Dover , external - the heartbreaking 1970 tale of an abandoned mother giving birth to a stillborn child was controversial and Wagoner warned Parton against releasing it

The Bargain Store , external - a moving lyrical account of a lady, experienced in love and loss, comparing herself to a secondhand shop, from 1975

Here You Come Again , external - written by Barry Mann and Cynthia Weil and released by Parton in 1977, it saw her skillfully pivot to pop/soft rock to great effect on her first big crossover hit

articles.title: Jewish, Muslim, Christian Jerusalem Old City vendors say reduced tourism is harming businesses
articles.summary: Vendors pointed to a shortage of flights, high airfares, and lingering fears abroad about security as the main reasons traffic into Israel has suffered. Shop...
articles.body:
Vendors pointed to a shortage of flights, high airfares, and lingering fears abroad about security as the main reasons traffic into Israel has suffered.

Shopkeepers across the Jewish, Muslim, Christian, and Armenian quarters of Jerusalem's Old City say the weakened state of inbound tourism to Israel over the last three years, since the outbreak of war, has put businesses under prolonged strain.

Speaking this week to The Jerusalem Post , vendors pointed to a shortage of flights, high airfares, and lingering fears abroad over security as chief reasons traffic into Israel has been suffering.

"The day-to-day tourism is horrible," Eitan, the owner of Mira, a family-owned shop in the Jewish Quarter, said. "Not too many people. There's not the traffic that there should be."

The main problem, he said, was that there were a reduced number of flights and that the flights that were operating were too expensive for many people, and people are afraid to come."

"I know a lot of people who cancel their — like, sometimes the airline canceled their trip, sometimes they could not come because of the prices," he said. "Once you have limited seats available, not everybody can come."

Eitan, whose family has lived in the Old City since 1968, operated the business since 1984, and has been through "all the intifadas" and "all the wars," said that a meaningful recovery from the tourism slump will remain out of sight until the situation with the airlines improves.

"As long as the airlines are not coming back to Israel, I don't see any solution," he said.

Similar concerns were voiced elsewhere in the Old City.

Dia, a long-time vendor in Jerusalem's Old City Arab Quarter whose family operates the well-known "Alabama – The Heart of Dixie" shop, said the decline in tourism had left business "very, very slow," with many visitors still hesitant to come because of the war.

"It's very safe, the Old City," he said, but due to the image Israel has had abroad since the war began on October 7, 2023, business remained low.

"Three years now, nobody comes," he said.

Hassan, a souvenir vendor near the Church of the Holy Sepulcher in Jerusalem's Christian Quarter, also painted a negative picture, describing business as "very weak" and saying there were "no tourists now."

He recalled that before the war broke out, there was a period of eight to ten months when business was good, "but now, it's zero."

Hassan continued, saying that in his view, the solution lay in bolstering the number of flights coming into Israel.

In the Armenian Quarter, Garo Sandrouni, who operates a ceramics gallery with his wife, Sonia, said that even since the latest major round of strikes between Israel and Iran concluded earlier this year, he had not seen any improvement in the number of tourists coming through.

He said, though, that with the Jewish New Year coming up next month, vendors expected to see some progress.

"Now, everybody is expecting in September that it (the amount of inbound tourism) will be much more. Let's see. But now, there is not much difference from what it was like three months ago or four months ago."

Like other vendors, Garo pointed to the cost of flights as the primary barrier choking off tourism to the country.

"They're much more expensive than before, and some people are also afraid to come," he said.

Sandrouni added that the fear came from three places.

"People are afraid, first from the war, secondly from flights if they cancel, and thirdly from the expensive tickets," he said.

He recalled clients who became stranded in Israel after foreign carriers canceled service, with some eventually traveling to Jordan to fly home.

Sandrouni added that the hits his business has taken over the last three years have been the worst in his four decades of operations.

"I have been here for like 40, 45 years on this street," he said. "It is the worst thing that we have witnessed. I mean, from the October war until today."

Speaking to the Post in June, tourism expert Dr. Eran Ketter pointed to broad structural problems hampering inbound tourism to Israel.

Looking specifically at the US, historically Israel's largest source market, Ketter pointed to geopolitical instability, the stronger shekel, limited air capacity, and higher travel costs as factors suppressing demand.

Tourism expert: Problems around tourism limit visitors to just the highly committed

"Putting all of this together, we're coming into a situation that only people who really want to travel to Israel, and can afford it, are traveling at the moment," he said.

Ketter said greater political stability would be the "number one enabler," allowing the industry to move from a nearly three-year "survival state" into "growth mode."

Stability, he added, would also encourage airlines to resume service, bringing more competition and potentially cheaper fares.

Tourism Ministry Director-General Michael Izhakov , who spoke to the Post the following month, also identified the lack of flight accessibility as a major bottleneck to inbound tourism.

Tourism ministry director-general: With no flights, there is no tourism

"When there are no flights, there is no tourism," he said, adding that the ministry was speaking with airlines and the Transportation Ministry and expected a rapid recovery once flights returned.

"We are waiting only for the flights," he said. "Once the flights reopen, we will see a very rapid recovery in inbound tourism to Israel."

The ministry has also been trying to stimulate demand through marketing and domestic tourism while preparing additional hotel capacity. Izhakov said the ministry had begun targeting Jewish audiences abroad more directly and had shifted some attention toward Israeli tourists when foreign visitors failed to return.

Earlier this month, Izhakov and tourism industry leaders met US Ambassador Mike Huckabee as part of the Israel Tourism Recovery Forum, where, according to the ministry, they discussed expanding direct US-Israel flights.

During the meeting, Huckabee emphasized his personal commitment to promote trips from the US to Israel.

"I will continue encouraging Americans to visit Israel, experience it firsthand, and discover the reality for themselves," the ministry quoted the ambassador as saying.

For the vendors in the Old City who depend on this traffic, though, the recovery of inbound tourism and the expansion of flights into the country are things they say cannot wait.

Still, despite the economic situation they described, some remained optimistic.

"I'm a positive person," Eitan said. "I believe things will be good again. When, we don't know, but hopefully soon. We are here, and whatever God wants to give us, he gives us."

articles.title: She Posed as a Federal Attorney and Charged a Family Nearly $40,000. Court Records Say They Missed Eight Hearings
articles.summary: An Indiana woman with a prior fraud conviction and two other pending cases is facing a new charge after authorities say she posed as a... Read More
articles.body:
An Indiana woman with a prior fraud conviction and two other pending cases is facing a new charge after authorities say she posed as a federal attorney and collected tens of thousands of dollars from a family seeking help with a Fort Wayne code enforcement dispute.

Katherine Jackson, 42, formerly of Newburgh, allegedly told the family she was licensed to practice law and worked with established law firms in Fort Wayne and Chicago. Police later contacted both firms and were told she had never worked for either one.

Court records say the family paid Jackson more than $34,000 for supposed legal work, consulting services and other expenses while believing she was handling their case.

The arrangement left them with another problem. Eight Neighborhood Code Compliance hearings were held without anyone appearing on their behalf, with each missed hearing carrying a $300 fee, according to 14 News .

She Claimed She Was a Licensed Federal Attorney

The latest case began after a man told police in July that Jackson had offered to represent his family in a dispute with Fort Wayne Neighborhood Code Compliance.

According to 21Alive , the man wanted to pursue what he believed were unwarranted code enforcement fees in federal court. Jackson, an acquaintance, allegedly told him she was a federal attorney, claimed she had passed a law exam and showed him what she represented as her scores.

She also claimed to work for Samuel Bolinger and Associates in Fort Wayne and Prusak and Harkins in Chicago. Investigators later contacted both firms and were told Jackson had never been employed by them. Court records also say she was not licensed as an attorney in Indiana or Illinois.

The Family Paid for Depositions, Audits and Consultants

Investigators say the family made payments for supposed depositions, audits, emails, copies and other legal work. Some payments were made by check or cash, while others were charged through Full Circle Auto, a business associated with Jackson.

She allegedly told the family they also needed a media consulting company and a real estate consultant. Court records say she represented that the media agreement would cost $5,000 and sought money for the other consultant's airfare, hotel and professional fees.

Police later contacted the companies. The media firm said an agreement bearing the family's name appeared to have been altered, while the real estate consultant said he had never heard of Jackson or the family and had never had an Indiana client.

Jackson is charged with one count of fraud in the attorney-impersonation case and was being held at the Allen County Jail when the charge was announced. The attorney-impersonation charge remains pending and has not resulted in a conviction.

They Went to Federal Court and Discovered No Case Had Been Filed

Jackson allegedly appeared with the family at a Neighborhood Code Compliance hearing in February 2024 and then told them they did not need to attend future hearings. Eight later hearings proceeded without the family or anyone acting on their behalf, according to court records.

The situation came to a head after Jackson allegedly told them their federal case was going to trial June 8 at the federal courthouse in Fort Wayne. When the family arrived, they could not find Jackson, a case number or any record of the proceeding they had been expecting. They learned that no federal case had been filed on their behalf, according to 21Alive. Investigators say Jackson stopped communicating with them afterward.

A Separate $8,000 Car Case Is Also Pending

Jackson was charged in another fraud case in July after a man accused her of taking $8,000 to purchase a vehicle that he never received. Earlier reporting says Jackson told the man she owned a car lot and held a dealer's license that would allow her to buy a 2017 Smart Fortwo at a better price.

After receiving the money, she allegedly blamed the delay on repairs and tariffs and asked for additional funds. The man contacted the Virginia dealership advertising the vehicle and learned it had instead been sold to someone in New York.

She Is Awaiting Trial in a Case Involving Her Daughter

Jackson also faces two neglect charges and a fraud charge filed in 2025 following an investigation into representations about her daughter's health.

Investigators said a GoFundMe raised more than $1,500 while describing the child as having Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, suffering dozens of seizures each day and having only months to live. The family also received a Make-A-Wish trip.

A physician who reviewed the child's records concluded there had been extensive maternal falsification and possible medical child abuse, according to court documents. Another doctor said the child does have Pilarowski-Bjornsson syndrome, but described the genetic disorder as chronic rather than terminal.

Jackson's attorneys have disputed the state's allegations and said she did not lie about her daughter's illness to obtain support. That case is scheduled for trial in January.

An Earlier Fundraising Case Resulted in a Conviction

Jackson's older Warrick County case has a different legal status because it ended in a guilty plea. More than a decade ago, while using the name Katherine Conapinski, she was accused of misrepresenting an organization while collecting money connected to a boy with cancer, including funds collected at his funeral.

Jackson accepted a plea agreement and initially received five years of probation, one year of home detention and an order requiring up to $20,000 in restitution. Court records later showed that she violated probation and was sentenced to four years in prison.

Verify a Lawyer's License Before Paying Legal Fees

The Indiana Judicial Branch Roll of Attorneys is the official roster of people licensed to practice law in the state. Consumers can search by name and review an attorney's licensing status rather than relying on business cards, claimed exam scores, contracts or documents provided by the person offering representation.

Clients should also ask for the case number after a lawsuit is filed and independently verify that the case exists. Indiana's MyCase system provides public access to many state court cases, while federal filings can be verified through the appropriate federal court or the federal PACER system.

Unexpected requests for repeated payments for consultants, filing expenses or other services should be accompanied by documentation that can be independently confirmed. If a purported lawyer cannot provide a verifiable license, court case or connection to the law firm they claim to represent, stop sending money until those claims are checked.

articles.title: CIA Director John Ratcliffe on secret trip in Russia
articles.summary: A U.S. Air Force Boeing C-17A Globemaster III transport plane was spotted at a Moscow airport, along with a U.S. diplomatic motorcade, according to public re...
articles.body:
CIA Director John Ratcliffe is in Moscow, Russia, for meetings, sources familiar with the situation told CBS News on Tuesday.

News of his trip comes after a U.S. Air Force Boeing C-17A Globemaster III transport plane was spotted at a Moscow airport, along with a U.S. diplomatic motorcade. Neither the U.S. nor Russian governments has commented on the identity of the U.S. official in Russia or the purpose of the visit.

It appears to be Ratcliffe's first known trip to Russia as CIA director, though he has maintained contact with Russian intelligence counterparts.

Ahead of Ratcliffe's trip, the U.S. told Ukraine that a senior delegation would be traveling to Moscow and asked it to suspend strikes until the delegation's departure, according to a senior Ukrainian official.

Ratcliffe's visit comes as recent U.S. intelligence assessments indicate that Putin's risk calculus may be shifting, with the Russian leader potentially increasingly willing to authorize provocative actions against NATO members — including hybrid operations and other deniable measures short of conventional military action — in order to test the resolve of the alliance and the Trump administration.

At this time, U.S.-mediated peace talks with Ukraine remain mostly stalled, with the sides still far apart on core issues.

The CIA has played a role in recent U.S.-Russia detainee exchanges, including the April 2025 release of a U.S.-Russian dual national Ksenia Karelina , whose case Ratcliffe personally negotiated. The agency was also involved in the 2024 prisoner exchange that secured the release of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich and Marine veteran Paul Whelan.

Former CIA Director William Burns traveled to Moscow in November 2021, when he met with senior Russian officials and spoke directly with President Vladimir Putin to warn him against invading Ukraine.

articles.title: Former Fire Chief Put Department Debit Card on His Personal Cash App, Then Withdrew $6,500, OSBI Says
articles.summary: A former Oklahoma volunteer fire chief is accused of obtaining a debit card connected to his department’s bank account, linking it to his personal Cash... R...
articles.body:
A former Oklahoma volunteer fire chief is accused of obtaining a debit card connected to his department's bank account, linking it to his personal Cash App and using fire department money for himself.

Blake Kendall, 28, formerly served as volunteer fire chief in Mannsville.

The Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation says its probe uncovered more than $1,200 in transactions through his personal Cash App and a separate $6,500 cash withdrawal from Citizens Bank.

Agents also identified other reported cash withdrawals and debit card purchases totaling more than $7,800, according to KXII . Kendall was arrested Aug. 24 in Ardmore and now faces charges of embezzlement and violations of the Oklahoma Computer Crimes Act.

Investigators Say He Linked the Department Card to His Cash App

The investigation began after the Carter County District Attorney's Office asked the OSBI to examine allegations of embezzlement, fraud and computer crime involving the City of Mannsville.

Agents with the agency's Fraud and Cybercrime Unit identified Kendall as a suspect and reviewed financial activity involving the volunteer fire department. According to the OSBI, Kendall obtained a debit card tied to the department's bank account and added it to his personal Cash App. T

Investigators separately identified a $6,500 cash withdrawal from Citizens Bank. The OSBI also reported several other cash withdrawals and debit card purchases totaling more than $7,800.

He Faces Embezzlement and Computer Crime Charges

During the investigation, authorities determined that Kendall is a Chickasaw citizen. The OSBI provided its investigative report to the Chickasaw Lighthorse Police Department and the Chickasaw Nation Office of Tribal Justice Administration. Chickasaw Lighthorse Police arrested Kendall in Ardmore on Aug. 24. He was then booked into the Marshall County Jail.

Kendall was arrested on allegations of embezzlement and violations of the Oklahoma Computer Crimes Act. Kendall has not been convicted. The charges remain accusations and will proceed through the applicable court process.

Public Debit Cards Need Independent Oversight

Organizations entrusted with public money can reduce the opportunity for misuse by separating control of payment cards from responsibility for reviewing the transactions.

The U.S. Government Accountability Office's internal-control standards emphasize preventive controls that safeguard public resources. Those controls include separating incompatible responsibilities so one person does not control authorization, spending and review.

Unexplained cash withdrawals, transfers to personal payment apps and transactions without supporting documentation should receive prompt review. Access should also be removed when an official or employee no longer needs a card, and organizations can use transaction alerts and limits to flag unusual activity before losses accumulate.

When suspected misuse is discovered, financial statements, card records, Cash App or other payment-service records, receipts and authorization documents should be preserved for auditors and investigators.

articles.title: Elissa Slotkin calls out Hasan Piker for blaming Jewish Americans targeted over their Israel views
articles.summary: Hasan Piker warned that American Jews could face violence over Israel support, prompting senators Elissa Slotkin and Jacky Rosen to condemn his remarks.
articles.body: Democratic Sens. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., and Jacky Rosen, D-Nev., condemned livestreamer Hasan Piker after he said that Jewish Americans will face inevitable consequences for supporting Israel. Last week, Piker told his viewers, "If Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they are singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone is going to come around and take action, not against the state of Israel, mind you, but against American Jews." Slotkin, who is widely believed to be a potential contender for the 2028 presidential election, shared what she called a "response to Hasan Piker's recent comments on Jews in America being targeted because of their views on Israel." "This shouldn’t be hard: no community should face the threat [of] violence for their political views. Period," Slotkin shared in a statement posted to social media. "That goes if you’re pro-Israel, pro-Palestine, pro-choice, pro-life or any other cause you care about. And blaming the victims of violence for bringing it on themselves only further endangers people." ANTISEMITIC STREAMER FINALLY MAKES DEM LEADER SNAP WITH RARE REBUKE: ‘MALICIOUS’ She suggested that this is part of a much larger phenomenon of the normalization of political violence. "In a time where political violence and anti-semitism has been spiking — and where just 6 months ago Michigan had a nearly deadly event of anti-semitic mass violence at Temple Israel — no one should causally be suggesting that anyone, Jews or otherwise, are to blame for being targeted," Slotkin concluded. Rosen offered a similar statement, blasting Piker’s remarks as "a new low." "Hasan Piker has been trafficking in antisemitic tropes for a while but even this is a new low," she posted to X. "Blaming Jewish Americans for the violence and hate they’re facing is not just wrong, it provides an excuse to those perpetuating these anti-Jewish hate crimes. Let me be absolutely clear: crimes against Jews for being Jews is antisemitism plain and simple. There’s no excuse for it." ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE REACHES DEADLIEST LEVEL SINCE 1994, NEW GLOBAL REPORT FINDS Many prominent politicians across the aisle, including fellow Democrats, have spoken out directly against Piker, arguing that he appears to be victim-blaming the Jewish community for attacks they endure. While Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed has previously shrugged off Piker’s controversial remarks, he appeared to distance himself from the left-wing streamer after the latest controversy. Piker has a long history of controversial comments, ranging from saying "America deserved 9/11" to praising a Zohran Mamdani administration official’s desire to "’impoverish the White middle-class.’" CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached out to representatives for Hasan Piker and did not immediately receive a response.

articles.title: As Ukraine hits Russia's refineries, Russia targets Ukraine's petrol pumps
articles.summary: Fuel companies are urging customers not to linger at the pumps after a wave of deadly attacks.
articles.body:
"Fill up quickly and move on," Mayor Ihor Terekhov warns drivers in Ukraine's second largest city Kharkiv.

Two petrol stations in the city in Ukraine's north-east were hit by Russian drones on Monday, which local officials say wounded two people. In another attack on a petrol station outside the city of Kryvyi Rih last week, three people were killed.

Russia's campaign of targeting civilian filling stations with drones and missiles began in earnest in April, primarily in regions on the front line, and the attacks are steadily growing more frequent.

At the same time, Russia has endured two waves of severe fuel shortages across the country as a result of Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries.

In total, Russia has hit at least 246 filling stations across Ukraine so far, says Oleksandr Sirenko, an analyst with Ukrainian energy think-tank Nafto Rynok ("Oil Market").

In July alone, the Centre for Information Resilience, an open-source investigation non-profit group, verified 114 Russian strikes on filling stations, compared with 66 the month before.

Given the threat, police have issued special guidance urging motorists to leave petrol stations and, if necessary, to abandon their vehicles whenever air raid alerts sound.

"You can fix your car, but you won't get your life back," says one police force in the Dnipropetrovsk region.

The damage is highly disruptive and puts civilians at considerable risk.

According to Sirenko, initially the attacks were being carried out with smaller, remote-controlled drones, but then Russia started using bigger, more expensive and more destructive Iranian-made Shahed drones.

One Shahed drone is estimated to cost between $20,000 (£14,500) and $50,000 (£36,000).

"One petrol station took five Shahed hits," Sirenko tells the BBC. "These Shaheds cost more than the petrol station."

Some key roads have no functioning petrol stations left, such as the road linking the two major cities of Kharkiv and Dnipro.

All the petrol stations have been destroyed around Opishnya, a large village in neighbouring Poltava region.

"You can see our enemy's strategy. They want to deprive us of fuel," says village chief Mykola Riznyk. In a video on Facebook, he says local authorities have begun stocking up on fuel, keeping small amounts of it in different locations.

In Mykolaiv in southern Ukraine, local resident and driver Kateryna Stokolya says petrol stations everywhere are becoming far stricter about not working during air alerts.

"Now everyone's making allowances for that, and it's not a problem," she tells the BBC. "Security comes first. If you can't fill up now, you'll fill up later. There are no queues or panic buying."

Stokolya believes that, in carrying out attacks of this nature, Russia's intended goal is "terrorising the public so we force the government to capitulate or accept agreements that do not favour Ukraine".

In Ukrainian-controlled areas of the partly occupied Kherson region, almost half the petrol stations have stopped working. The others get attacked by Russian drones "almost every day", says deputy regional administration head Oleksandr Tolokonnikov.

All petrol stations have reportedly been destroyed in Trostyanets, a town of almost 20,000 people near the north-eastern border with Russia. In response, local authorities started dispensing fuel straight from road tankers which keep changing their location to minimise the chances of being hit.

Ukrainians appear to be heeding the advice of authorities.

"Clients aren't browsing the aisles anymore, looking at what we've got on our shelves," says Oleksandr Melnychuk, head of the strategic marketing department at BRSM Nafta chain of petrol stations. "They fill up and are keen to get on their way as soon as possible."

His company has lost eight petrol stations and is rebuilding another two after they were hit.

To protect customers, BRSM Nafta has been building concrete shelters at its forecourts and also covering them in anti-drone nets. It has also shortened working hours and reduced the number of staff present in some locations.

However, so far the drone strikes have not had a dramatic impact on fuel supplies. According to a report by the National Bank of Ukraine, 4% of the country's filling stations have been damaged or destroyed, but the impact on the market has been small.

"Increasing sales in regions which are further away from the front line or from the border with Russia have made up for sales lost at destroyed stations," the report says.

The picture in Russia is very different, after Ukraine's campaign of attacks on Russian refineries and other infrastructure.

Russia has seen fuel shortages in almost every region as a result. One popular newspaper in Russia, Izvestia, said last week that petrol was only available at 28% of Russian filling stations.

Unlike in Russia, Ukraine does not rely on vulnerable large refineries and fuel depots, instead importing fuel by road using tanker trucks.

Ukraine's market is also saturated with numerous petrol stations, which usually offer drivers alternatives should one or several of them be targeted in a particular area, Sirenko says.

"You curse and drive on to another petrol station. OK, you travel for 10km more than you bargained for, but that's not such a big problem," he says.

If anything, it is the war between the US and Iran that is having a bigger impact on local fuel prices, he says. Normally, the most expensive parts of filling stations are left undamaged by Russian attacks, such as petrol and diesel tanks underground.

articles.title: Mom Tells 6-Year-Old Shaving Her Head Would Make the Hair Grow ‘Quicker,’ but 30 Years Later, It Never Grew Back (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Holly Faller, 35, spent years imagining she’d have hair by high school, graduation or even her wedding before realizing it wasn’t coming back
articles.body:
Holly Faller, 35, was 6 and already experiencing significant hair loss from alopecia when her mom tried an old wives' tale in hopes of helping

Although she began wearing wigs as a child, Holly remained convinced that her own hair would eventually return

More than three decades later, her relationship with being bald looks very different from the one she imagined as a little girl

For most of her childhood, Holly never pictured herself growing up bald. She pictured starting high school with hair, then graduating with it and, when neither happened, she became certain it would at least be there by the time she got married.

"As a young child, I only imagined myself starting high school with hair," Holly Faller tells PEOPLE exclusively. "As a teenager, I only imagined having hair at high school graduation. And even after graduating, I assumed my hair would at least come back by the time I got married."

That certainty stretched back to when Holly was 6, after small bald patches she'd had from a young age continued to grow larger. By then, so little hair remained that she describes it now as just a few "scraggly" tufts clinging to her head.

In a recent TikTok , the 35-year-old took viewers back to that time, first sharing a childhood photo of herself with hair before revealing the story behind what became her last haircut. "My mum shaved off all my hair when I was 6?!" she wrote, acknowledging that the confession sounded more dramatic than the reality.

Her mom had exhausted other options and wanted to do anything she could to help her daughter when she turned to an old wives' tale that cutting her hair could make it grow back faster. To 6-year-old Holly, there was no reason to question it.

"As a kid, I was very trusting, and I believed all adults knew everything," she says. "So, when my mum told me that 'hair grows quicker if you cut it,' I thought, well, of course we should do that then!"

Her mom shaved off what remained, but the hoped-for regrowth never came. Holly jokes in the TikTok that she could blame her mom for her baldness, before quickly setting the record straight: She would have been bald whether her mom shaved her head or not.

Holly has alopecia, an autoimmune condition that causes hair loss, and had already lost most of her hair before the clippers ever came out. Shaving the remaining tufts made so little difference to her appearance that Holly says it wasn't a particularly difficult decision at the time.

"I think Mum was really hoping it could be true; she just wanted to do anything she could to help me," Holly says. Her mom has since told her that after trying other options, shaving her daughter's head felt like the only option left.

Afterward, Holly put on a wig and carried on with school and childhood, remembering herself as a happy-go-lucky kid who tended to "roll with the punches." She didn't want to be bald, but she couldn't change it, and she remained convinced that what she was experiencing was temporary.

The years that followed slowly challenged that belief. High school arrived, then graduation, marriage and her first job, and the hair Holly had pictured alongside each new version of herself never did.

"Every big life milestone I reached, still bald, brought new grief," she says. "When I graduated, when I got married, when I got my first job ... each time I had to grieve my hair loss all over again."

By her early 20s, Holly began to understand that the hair she'd been waiting for since she was 6 wasn't coming back. The realization was devastating in part because she'd spent years attaching its return to the life she wanted to live.

"I wanted hair so that I could finally put myself out there with confidence, and I just sat on the sideline while I waited," she says. "I continued to hide myself away, thinking I couldn't live life to the full without hair."

Her outlook began to change after she joined online support groups for women with alopecia and found herself captivated by women who looked like her doing things she hadn't given herself permission to do. Seeing their lives challenged the belief she'd carried for years that she needed hair before her own could really begin.

"I used to believe that I wasn't complete without hair and that my life couldn't truly start until mine grew back," she says. "The women I was watching online proved to me that hair had absolutely nothing to do with it."

Still, there was a difference between showing her bald head online and letting strangers see it in the real world. Wigs had been Holly's "safety blanket" since childhood, and putting one on before leaving home eventually felt as ordinary as putting on shoes.

That began to shift at her birthday party last year, when Holly gave guests an unusual dress code: Anyone who wasn't already bald had to wear a bald cap. Holly covered her own head in rhinestones, and soon her friends were bedazzling their bald caps to match.

"I saw 'bald' through a totally different lens that night," she says. "Bald was suddenly something fun."

Most of the guests had seen Holly without a wig before, but she'd never been bald in front of such a large group at once. Instead of feeling like something she needed to conceal, her baldness became part of the celebration, with friends complimenting her rhinestones and how they matched her dress.

"It just made my baldness seem 'cool,' " she says. "It made me feel just a little more ready to face the world as a bald girl."

Holly documented what came next in a separate TikTok , explaining that after more than 30 years of wearing wigs every day, she'd made going bald in public her New Year's resolution. Her first attempt wasn't a restaurant, vacation or crowded night out; she started by taking the bins to the street.

From there came walks, cafes, restaurants, an interstate weekend and even a trip to the club with fellow bald friends. But on one of those early walks with her partner, Ryan, Holly was still so aware of being without a wig that every car and pedestrian seemed to prompt the same question.

"Every car that drove past us, every person that walked across the street, I'd say to Ryan, 'Do you think they know I'm bald?' " she recalls. "I was sure that any second, a car would accidentally run off the road due to my bald head distracting their driver."

The reality was considerably quieter. Holly says the experience was "actually all very unclimactic," and while she avoids looking for every stranger's reaction, the ones that have reached her directly have been kind, including older women complimenting her rhinestones at a cafe and retail assistants praising her look.

"The best way I can describe this to non-bald people is that it feels like going out naked," she says. Even now, going bald can require some mental preparation, while a wig remains the familiar option that doesn't require a second thought.

Holly hasn't stopped wearing wigs, nor does she want to. She still considers them a source of security and comfort, and when she's getting glammed up for a night with friends, her 26-inch blonde wig might be exactly what she wants.

What has changed is that she no longer feels she has to put one on every time she steps outside. "In the last year it has shifted from a necessity to an option," she says.

It's a choice Holly couldn't have imagined as the little girl who kept waiting for her hair to return before the rest of her life could begin. If she could speak to that 6-year-old now, she'd tell her there was never anything she needed to wait for.

"I would tell 6-year-old Holly that hair was never needed for her to be complete," she says. "She didn't have to hold herself back, missing out on things, waiting until she had hair."

Um acidente entre duas motos e um caminhão causou lentidão na Avenida José Joaquim de Lacerda, na zona norte de Sorocaba (SP), na manhã desta quarta-feira (26).

Segundo apurado pela TV TEM, os motociclistas tiveram escoriações e foram socorridos com ferimentos leves.

articles.title: Caminhão quebra e trava trânsito na Avenida Centenário em Piracicaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso foi registrado no início da manhã desta quarta-feira (26) na Avenida Centenário. Nenhuma equipe da Semuttran monitorava o trecho até às 8h20.
articles.summary: Caminhão quebrado em Piracicaba trava a Avenida Centenário e motoristas improvisam sinalização com baldes diante da ausência de agentes de trânsito.
articles.body:
Um caminhão carregado com cinco toneladas de farinha de mandioca quebrou na Avenida Cententário, em frente ao campus da Universidade de São Paulo (Esalq-USP) em Piracicaba (SP) por volta das 7h desta quarta-feira (26). O veículo teve um problema mecânico. Há congestionamento no local.

Até às 8h desta quarta-feira (26), nenhuma equipe da Secretaria Municipal de Segurança Pública, Trânsito e Transportes (Semuttran) estava no local do incidente. Quem frequenta o trecho improvisou sinalização com pedaços de madeira e balde.

Às 8h15, ainda havia lentidão no trânsito no trecho, que costuma ter fluxo intenso de automóveis, principalmente nos horários de pico.

Caminhão carregado com farinha quebra, trava trânsito e avenida é sinalizada com balde e madeira em Piracicaba — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

O caminhão está estacionado na esquina da Avenida Carlos Botelho. O motorista saía de Piracicaba e seguia sentido Campinas (SP).

O motorista afirmou que já acionou empresa responsável e aguarda chegada de mecânico para consertar caminhão e poder liberar a via.

Caminhão carregado com 5 tonelads de farinha quebra na Avenida Centenário em Piracicaba e via tem sinalização improvisada com balde e pedaços de madeira — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/Reprodução

Os motoristas que chegam em Piracicaba pela ponte do Shopping podem desviar pela Avenida Renato Vagner.

Essa é a segunda ocorrência de caminhão quebrado em via de Piracicaba. Na última segunda-feira (24), um outro caminhão carregado com 25 toneladas de sucata também teve uma pene mecânica e travou o trânsito na Rodovia Geraldo de Barros (SP-304).

articles.title: Dirigente de ensino afastada após recomendar biografias de Hitler | G1
articles.standfirst: Roselaine Batalha Silva fez as declarações durante reunião virtual com diretores de escolas de Mogi das Cruzes; Secretaria de Educação abriu apuração sobre o caso.
articles.summary: A dirigente de ensino afastada em Mogi das Cruzes classificou Hitler como líder excepcional em reunião; a Secretaria da Educação de SP abriu apuração sobre o caso.
articles.body:
Roselaine Batalha Silva deixou a função de dirigente da Unidade Regional de Ensino de Mogi das Cruzes após recomendar a diretores de escolas a leitura das biografias de Adolf Hitler e Benito Mussolini durante uma reunião virtual.

✅ Clique para seguir o canal do g1 Mogi das Cruzes e Suzano no WhatsApp

A reunião foi realizada em 12 de agosto. Na gravação, Roselaine discutiu o conceito de liderança e citou livros e líderes de regimes autoritários do século 20 como exemplos de leituras “estimulantes”.

"No geral é estimulante ler biografia mesmo dos maus. Salazar na Espanha, Mussolini na Itália, Hitler. Mein Kampf [Minha Luta], 'Minha Vida' do Hitler, é tão estimulante que se eu tirar o nome ele convence países, jovens e nós até hoje", afirmou a dirigente aos gestores.

Durante a reunião, a dirigente também afirmou que Hitler era um “líder excepcional”, apesar de reconhecer o caminho seguido pelo ditador alemão.

"Mas a gente sabe qual era o caminho de Hitler, mas ele era um líder excepcional e isso ninguém pode negar. Mas não foi dada uma coroa para ele, mas a quem foi dada a responsabilidade de fazer sobressair o melhor que há nos outros. Esse é o meu diretor", declarou na reunião.

Dirigente de ensino de SP recomenda biografia de Hitler para diretores de escola — Foto: Reprodução

Em nota, a Secretaria Estadual de Educação informou que determinou o fim da função de dirigente exercida pela servidora. A pasta também instaurou uma apuração para verificar os fatos e as circunstâncias relacionadas às declarações.

A Secretaria afirmou ainda que não compactua com manifestações que contrariem os princípios e valores que orientam a educação pública do Estado de São Paulo. Segundo a pasta, as declarações não representam seu posicionamento.

Um dos diretores da rede estadual de ensino de Mogi das Cruzes, que pediu para não ser identificado, afirmou ao g1 que declarações desse tipo eram recorrentes nas reuniões conduzidas pela dirigente, realizadas às quartas-feiras.

“Tudo que aconteceu é real. Aliás, essas falas dela eram bem comuns”, contou.

O g1 procurou Roselaine Batalha Silva para comentar a decisão e as declarações feitas durante a reunião, mas não recebeu resposta até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: GWM anuncia o SUV híbrido Tank 400 para enfrentar o Toyota SW4 | G1
articles.standfirst: O jipão é o segundo modelo lançado da linha Tank, mas se destaca pelo motor mais potente, porte maior e foco no luxo, deixando as aptidões para o uso fora de estrada em segundo plano.
articles.summary: O jipão é o segundo modelo lançado da linha Tank, mas se destaca pelo motor mais potente, porte maior e foco no luxo, deixando as aptidões para o uso off-road em segundo plano.
articles.body:
A GWM anunciou o Tank 400, um jipão de sete lugares, maior que o Haval H9 e que chega ao mercado como híbrido plug-in para disputar a atenção de consumidores que já consideram o Toyota SW4.

À primeira vista, o Tank 400 não tem o mesmo visual totalmente quadrado do Haval H9 e do Tank 300 . Suas linhas são mais suaves e aproximam o modelo da proposta adotada pela Toyota em seu SUV grande.

O Tank 400 também traz alguns elementos que lembram o SW4, como a linha lateral que sobe ao chegar ao fim das portas traseiras e segue mais alta na janela logo atrás.

A grade frontal integrada aos faróis, posicionados mais acima, também lembra a do SW4. Nas dimensões, porém, o Tank 400 chega a ser 19 centímetros mais longo:

Comprimento: 4,98 metros (contra 4,79 metros do SW4);

Largura: 1,95 metro (contra 1,85 metro do SW4);

Altura: 1,9 metro (contra 1,83 metro do SW4);

Distância entre-eixos: 2,85 metros (contra 2,74 metros do SW4).

Para não dizer que o Tank 400 foi totalmente inspirado no SW4, o porta-malas abre para o lado e traz o estepe preso à tampa.

Por dentro, a comparação com o SUV que reina sozinho no segmento perde força, e o lado chinês aflora. Enquanto o SW4 é mais prático e menos requintado, o Tank 400 aposta em materiais mais macios ao toque, acabamento com cores menos contrastantes e uma lista de equipamentos mais ampla.

O destaque é a central multimídia posicionada acima do console central, com 16,3 polegadas, ao lado do painel digital de 12,3 polegadas. No SW4, o quadro de instrumentos ainda tem mostradores analógicos, e a central multimídia mede 9 polegadas. Abaixo do console, o Tank 400 traz dois carregadores de celular por indução

articles.title: Noiva realiza sonho de chegar a casamento montada em égua, em Goiás | G1
articles.standfirst: Thályta de Almeida Barros Kavaliauskis contou sobre a sua relação com Arizona, animal que participou do momento especial para a família. Cerimônia aconteceu em uma chácara em Goiânia.
articles.summary: Thályta de Almeida Barros Kavaliauskis contou sobre a sua relação com Arizona, animal que participou do momento especial para a família. Cerimônia aconteceu em uma chácara.
articles.body:
A noiva Thályta de Almeida Barros Kavaliauskis, de 21 anos, realizou o sonho de entrar em seu casamento montada em uma égua, em Goiânia (veja acima) . Em entrevista ao g1 , a designer de moda contou sobre a sua relação com Arizona, animal que participou do momento especial para a família.

"Sempre fui uma menina apaixonada por cavalos, meus tios me levavam muito para a chácara deles desde pequena e lá eu apartava vaca, andava muito a cavalo. Acabei me apaixonando por cavalo por conta dos meus primos", relatou.

✅ Clique e siga o canal do g1 GO no WhatsApp

A égua pertence ao primo dela, Patrick de Almeida. A ideia surgiu após a noiva ver um vídeo no Instagram e mandar uma mensagem para ele perguntando sobre a possibilidade de entrar com Arizona no casamento. Inicialmente, ele achou que ela estava brincando, mas no final deu tudo certo.

"Eu acompanhei o crescimento da Arizona desde que o Patrick a pegou, tenho familiaridade com ela. Então, começamos a pensar e planejar a entrada", disse.

Thályta de Almeida Barros Kavaliauskis é apaixonada por cavalos desde criança — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Thályta de Almeida Barros Kavaliauskis | Mariana Zurc

A cerimônia ocorreu no dia 15 de agosto, em uma chácara na capital. Thályta se casou com o engenheiro de software, Gabriel Cândido Kavaliauskis, de 26 anos.

"Poucas pessoas sabiam, então foi uma surpresa. Quando tocou a marcha nupcial ninguém me achava, até que me viram na estrada montada na Arizona. Todo mundo ficou chocado porque ninguém esperava", detalhou Thályta.

Noiva entrou montada em égua durante casamento em Goiânia — Foto: Brayan Quiroga

A noiva contou que foram feitos alguns ensaios com a Arizona antes do casamento, utilizando cobertas para simular o peso do vestido. Segundo ela, a égua é muito tranquila e não se incomodou com a preparação. A equipe que trabalharia na cerimônia também combinou alguns cuidados para evitar que o animal se assustasse.

“Foi um super combinado de todos da equipe que estava trabalhando no casamento para ficarem afastados de mim, porque cavalos são muito sensíveis e se assustam com facilidade”, explicou.

Arizona está prenha e o filhote deve nascer em novembro. Como ela veio de Heitoraí , na região noroeste de Goiás, foi levada ao local um dia antes para que pudesse descansar e ficar tranquila no dia do casamento. As preparações também começaram cedo: ela tomou banho, teve a crina loira natural tonalizada e usou um shampoo com glitter que já está costumada.

A ideia de enfeitar a égua com fitas partiu de Laura Parruchiere, responsável pela beleza da noiva. Segundo Thályta, Arizona aceitou tranquilamente a proposta. “Ela ficou até o final do casamento e foi uma verdadeira atração. Ela é super mansinha", destacou.

Noiva chega a cavalo a casamento 'agro' e chama a atenção dos convidados; vídeo

Casamentos em cachoeira impressionam em Goiás: ‘Parece um conto de fadas’

Casal transforma casamento em explosão de cores e surpreende web

A presença de Arizona no casamento repercutiu redes sociais. A noiva contou que recebeu críticas por não ser uma escolha considerada tradicional. “Eu acho que a graça de ser autêntico é isso, é defender as suas ideias. O ser diferente é legal, fugir do padrão. E o meu casamento foi bem fora do padrão mesmo!”, afirmou.

Ela explicou que, por serem cristãos, o casal quis realizar uma cerimônia seguindo a fé, mas sem reproduzir um casamento tradicional. “Eu sempre tive comigo que não queria um casamento tradicional chato ou entediante que o pessoal comesse e fosse embora", disse.

Thályta e o noivo Gabriel — Foto: Brayan Quiroga

Para Thályta, ela teve o "casamento dos sonhos" . As tradicionais lapelas foram substituídas por broches, e o DJ deu lugar a um quarteto de cordas. A festa também contou com um totem para impressão de fotos na hora e sorvete à vontade.

O vestido da noiva foi desenhado e criado pela estilista Aline Couto. A noiva contou que também queria uma peça fora do padrão e, por isso, a estilista criou uma textura que lembrava drapeados feitos à mão, um por um. O véu também fugiu do tradicional. O casal tinha referências de casamentos italianos e decidiu adaptar as ideias ao próprio estilo, “abrasileirando” tudo.

A comida também foi pensada para fugir do formato tradicional. Os pratos foram preparados na hora, com uma mesa de frios e arroz carreteiro sendo feito em um caldeirão no meio da festa. Também foram servidos hambúrgueres e comida de boteco.

A identidade do casamento também teve forte participação da família. Os menus das mesas foram impressos em tecido, enquanto a avó da noiva costurou renda Paraíba ao redor. A identidade visual e os convites foram desenhados pelo primo. “Tudo a nossa família estava envolvida", contou Thályta.

Depois da cerimônia, a recepção teve música ao vivo, com voz e violão. Em seguida, os noivos terminaram de confeitar o bolo, feito pela avó materna da noiva, Luzia Alves. Além dos brindes levados pela família, os próprios convidados começaram a “doar” presentes e serviços para que a brincadeira continuasse.

As alianças foram entregues pelos avós paternos da noiva, que destacou a importância da família em diferentes momentos da celebração. O casal também decidiu mudar as entradas tradicionais da cerimônia, incluindo os pais e avós, padrinhos e apenas duas crianças.

“Foi um casamento dos sonhos, cheio da presença de Deus, muito além do que eu sonhei e ainda bem que foi diferente. Eu não me arrependo de nada e sei que daqui muitos anos ainda vou amar reviver por meio de fotos e vídeos", ressaltou a noiva.

articles.title: MPT processa Uber por cobrar taxa de motoristas para trabalhar | G1
articles.standfirst: Programa 'Passe para Motoristas', que permite acesso a corridas mediante pagamento, pode custar mais de R$ 1 mil por mês, segundo o Ministério Público do Trabalho. Órgão afirma que modelo pode gerar servidão por dívida e pede suspensão da cobrança.
articles.summary: Programa 'Passe para Motoristas', que permite acesso a corridas mediante pagamento, pode custar mais de R$ 1 mil por mês, segundo o Ministério Público do Trabalho.
articles.body:
Motorista de aplicativo, app, Uber, 99 — Foto: Maksim Goncharenok/Pexels

O Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) ajuizou uma ação civil pública contra a Uber do Brasil para suspender o programa "Passe para Motoristas", que cobra dos motoristas uma taxa para que eles possam aceitar corridas pelo aplicativo.

O órgão também pede a devolução dos valores pagos pelos trabalhadores e uma indenização de R$ 321 milhões por dano moral coletivo .

Lançado em 25 de maio deste ano em 12 cidades, o programa já está disponível em 29 municípios , segundo informações divulgadas pela própria Uber. Entre as cidades participantes estão Itabuna e Ilhéus , na Bahia.

A empresa afirma que pretende expandir o modelo para todo o país . De acordo com os termos do programa, o motorista pode adquirir um passe por período ou por ganhos. Na primeira modalidade, o pagamento dá direito ao uso do aplicativo por 24 ou 72 horas.

Na segunda, o motorista paga uma quantia e fica sem cobrança de taxa de serviço até atingir um determinado limite de faturamento.

O programa também prevê uma ativação automática após a conclusão da primeira viagem considerada elegível.

Em nota enviada ao g1 , a Uber negou as acusações feitas pelo MPT e afirmou que vai apresentar à Justiça as informações necessárias para explicar como funciona o programa.

A empresa também destacou que o juiz responsável pelo caso pediu cautela na análise dos argumentos apresentados pelo Ministério Público, que ainda precisam ser investigados.

A Uber disse que as acusações sobre endividamento dos motoristas, retenção de pagamentos e concentração do trabalho no aplicativo não podem ser tratadas como fatos comprovados neste momento.

Segundo a empresa, o “Passe para Motoristas” é uma alternativa ao modelo tradicional de cobrança de taxa por corrida e está sendo testado em diferentes cidades do país. ( veja abaixo o posicionamento completo )

Segundo o MPT, o principal problema está no fato de o trabalhador ter de pagar antecipadamente para ter acesso às condições previstas pelo programa , sem garantia de que conseguirá realizar corridas suficientes para recuperar o valor desembolsado.

Nos próprios termos do serviço, segundo o órgão, a Uber informa que a compra do passe não garante um número mínimo de viagens. As corridas também podem ser direcionadas pelo algoritmo a motoristas que não aderiram ao programa.

Para o Ministério Público do Trabalho, isso faz com que o risco da atividade seja transferido para o motorista. Caso ele não consiga realizar corridas suficientes, pode não recuperar o valor investido .

O procurador do trabalho Luiz Antonio Nascimento Fernandes, responsável pela ação, afirma que o mecanismo pode criar uma situação de dependência econômica e caracterizar servidão por dívida.

"O mecanismo de cobrança do Passe cria uma estrutura objetiva de endividamento permanente: o motorista que não possui saldo suficiente tem suas futuras remunerações retidas automática e integralmente pela Ré. Esse mecanismo perpetua a dependência econômica do trabalhador em relação à plataforma e replica, no ambiente digital, a estrutura de servidão por dívida”, afirma Fernandes na ação.

Segundo o procurador, quando o motorista não possui saldo suficiente, valores de suas futuras remunerações podem ser retidos para quitar o débito com a plataforma. Para o MPT, o mecanismo reproduziria, no ambiente digital, características de um sistema de servidão por dívida.

O órgão também afirma que os valores cobrados podem superar R$ 1 mil por mês , dependendo da modalidade utilizada e da frequência de trabalho do motorista.

MPT processa Uber em R$ 321 milhões por cobrar taxa de motoristas para trabalhar — Foto: Reprodução/Uber/MPT

MPT vê risco de fidelização dos motoristas

Outro ponto questionado pelo Ministério Público do Trabalho é o efeito do programa sobre a concorrência entre plataformas.

A avaliação do órgão é que, depois de pagar pelo passe, o motorista teria menos incentivo para trabalhar em outros aplicativos durante o período de validade da assinatura.

Isso ocorreria porque cada hora trabalhada em uma plataforma concorrente representaria um período em que o motorista não estaria utilizando o serviço pelo qual já pagou .

Para o MPT, o mecanismo funcionaria como uma espécie de fidelização indireta , mesmo sem uma cláusula formal de exclusividade.

O órgão também questiona as condições contratuais do programa. Segundo a ação, os termos são definidos unilateralmente pela Uber e permitem que a empresa altere as regras do Passe a qualquer momento e desative o benefício sem necessariamente devolver o valor pago pelo motorista.

Além da suspensão do programa, o MPT solicitou acesso ao código-fonte do algoritmo utilizado pela Uber.

O objetivo é investigar, entre outros pontos, os critérios utilizados para a distribuição das corridas, a formação dos preços, os mecanismos de precificação dinâmica e os valores efetivamente repassados aos motoristas.

Na avaliação do órgão, o acesso a essas informações é necessário para verificar como o funcionamento do algoritmo interfere na atividade dos trabalhadores e na dinâmica do programa.

"Trata-se de uma cobrança abusiva de valores pela Uber em face dos seus motoristas, valores que podem superar até R$ 1 mil por mês. Em quase todos os países do mundo, há uma regra que proíbe empresas ou agências de cobrarem valores dos empregados para que eles tenham acesso ao trabalho", afirmou Ilan Fonseca, coordenador nacional de combate às fraudes trabalhistas do MPT.

Segundo Fonseca, a cobrança pode configurar condição análoga à escravidão , hipótese que será analisada no processo.

A ação foi distribuída à 9ª Vara do Trabalho de Salvador (BA), que deverá analisar os pedidos apresentados pelo Ministério Público do Trabalho.

O MPT pede, entre outras medidas, a suspensão do programa, a restituição dos valores cobrados dos motoristas e o pagamento de R$ 321 milhões por dano moral coletivo .

A ação ainda será analisada pela Justiça, portanto, as alegações apresentadas pelo Ministério Público do Trabalho são objeto de contestação no processo e não representam, neste momento, uma decisão definitiva sobre a legalidade do programa.

"Em decisão proferida no último dia 20, o juiz titular da 9ª Vara do Trabalho de Salvador manifestou a necessidade de "cautela" e "prudência processual" na análise dos pedidos formulados pelo MPT (Ministério Público do Trabalho).

De acordo com o juiz Luciano Carreiro, a relevância do tema "não se confunde com a presença automática dos pressupostos necessários à concessão, sem contraditório, de todas as providências requeridas".

O magistrado lista, especificamente, "as alegações referentes ao endividamento dos prestadores, à retenção de créditos futuros, à concentração de atividade na plataforma, aos efeitos concorrenciais e às projeções econômicas" apresentadas pelos procuradores. "A relevância dessas questões recomenda sua investigação, mas não autoriza que sejam consideradas fatos definitivamente estabelecidos", afirma.

A Uber refuta as conclusões apresentadas pelo MPT na ação e vai fornecer à Justiça, no prazo legal, todas as informações necessárias para o esclarecimento das questões levantadas pelos procuradores, que são baseadas em concepções equivocadas sobre o funcionamento da plataforma e em posições ideológicas sobre a relação estabelecida pelos motoristas com o aplicativo.

O modelo de assinatura é praticado no setor de transporte individual privado de passageiros, há anos, por outros aplicativos em funcionamento no Brasil.

O Passe para Motoristas representa uma alternativa comercial ao modelo tradicional de taxa de serviço por viagem, em fase de testes pela Uber, com o objetivo de verificar sua aderência a contextos locais diversos, possibilitando oferecer aos parceiros previsibilidade antecipada sobre o custo do serviço de intermediação prestado pela plataforma dentro das condições definidas."

articles.title: El Niño atrasa chuvas no AP e acende alerta para seca e risco de queimadas, aponta Censipam | G1
articles.standfirst: Previsão do Censipam aponta precipitação abaixo da média de agosto a outubro. Estado deve registrar pancadas isoladas e temperaturas acima do normal.
articles.summary: Previsão do Censipam aponta precipitação abaixo da média de agosto a outubro. Estado deve registrar pancadas isoladas e temperaturas acima do normal.
articles.body:
El Niño volta ao Amapá em 2026, mas com impactos menos graves que na crise de 2023. — Foto: Rafael Aleixo/Arquivo g1

O Amapá e outros estados do centro-norte da Amazônia Legal enfrentam um cenário de chuvas abaixo da média histórica e temperaturas acima do normal ao longo do trimestre agosto-setembro-outubro (ASO).

O alerta consta no Boletim nº 2 do Painel El Niño (2026-2027) e indica riscos crescentes de deficiência hídrica no solo, pressão sobre o setor agropecuário e aumento severo de incêndios em vegetações rurais e urbanas.

✅ Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 AP no WhatsApp

Climatologicamente, o trimestre ASO marca o fim da estação seca e a transição para o período chuvoso na região.

No entanto, o fortalecimento do fenômeno El Niño, caracterizado pelo aquecimento das águas do Oceano Pacífico Equatorial, altera a circulação dos ventos e atrasa a chegada do chamado "inverno amazônico".

Segundo a previsão do Centro Gestor e Operacional do Sistema de Proteção da Amazônia (Censipam), o padrão para os próximos meses será marcado por precipitações mal distribuídas e intercaladas por longos períodos de estiagem:

🌧Chuvas isoladas : A precipitação ocorrerá por meio de episódios convectivos isolados (pancadas rápidas e locais), com acumulados mensais que podem ser inferiores a 20 mm durante o mês de agosto.

🌞Radiação solar e calor : A menor cobertura de nuvens associada à baixa umidade relativa do ar aumentará a incidência de radiação solar direta sobre o estado, elevando o desconforto térmico da população.

🌅Impacto no solo e rios : Os longos intervalos sem chuva impedem a recuperação da umidade do solo e limitam a recarga dos níveis de rios e igarapés amapaenses.

Apesar do alerta, o relatório aponta uma condição mais amena quando comparada ao ápice da crise do último super El Niño (biênio 2023/2024). Em junho de 2026, a intensidade da seca no Norte se mostrou menos severa do que no mesmo período de 2023.

O Monitor de Secas ressalta que não é possível fazer uma comparação em termos percentuais diretos para o Amapá e Roraima, pois ambos os estados ainda não faziam parte da rede de monitoramento à época.

No entanto, o mapeamento atual indica que estados vizinhos que registraram focos de "seca grave" em 2023 — como Amazonas, Acre e Rondônia — não apresentam a mesma severidade no ciclo atual.

Petrobras prevê investir US$ 2,5 bilhões em 15 poços na Margem Equatorial até 2030

Moradora perde casa em incêndio que atingiu 150 pessoas no AP: 'não aguento mais tanto sofrimento'

Impactos nos setores produtivos e ambientais

A persistência do tempo seco trará reflexos diretos na economia e no meio ambiente do Amapá. A falta de umidade deve afetar as pastagens e o manejo agrícola, além de pressionar o abastecimento de água em áreas mais vulneráveis.

O aumento do risco de queimadas exige atenção redobrada das autoridades ambientais e da população para evitar incêndios florestais e urbanos durante todo o período de estiagem.

articles.title: Dolly Parton: música inédita está em cápsula do tempo para 2045 | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantora, que morreu nesta terça (25), trancou faixa secreta em uma caixa com aparelhos de som. Em entrevistas, revelou medo de mídia se desintegrar antes do tempo.
articles.summary: Dolly Parton deixou uma música inédita em uma cápsula do tempo para 2045, temendo que a gravação secreta se desintegrasse antes de ser ouvida pelo público.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton deixou uma música inédita guardada em uma cápsula do tempo em Dollywood, parque temático criado pela cantora no Tennessee, nos Estados Unidos.

Durante uma participação no programa The Kelly Clarkson Show, em dezembro de 2022, Parton contou que escreveu e gravou uma música especialmente para ser colocada em uma cápsula criada para preservar memórias e objetos para o futuro. Ela a chamou de "Dream Box" (Caixa do Sonho).

“Você não tem ideia de como isso me incomodou. Quero muito desenterrá-la. É uma música muito boa”, revelou a Kelly Clarkson, na época.

Parton também explicou que colocou na caixa equipamentos para que a gravação pudesse ser reproduzida no futuro, incluindo um toca-fitas e um aparelho de CD. A preocupação, porém, passou a ser justamente a conservação do material.

“Eu fico pensando que ela pode simplesmente se desintegrar e ninguém nunca vai ouvi-la”, afirmou.

Dolly Parton durante entrevista ao programa The Kelly Clarkson Show, em 2022, quando comentou sobre a música inédita guardada em uma cápsula do tempo. — Foto: Reprodução/YouTube/Kelly Clarkson Show

A "Dream Box" foi criada para permanecer fechada até 2045, quando Parton completaria 99 anos. Segundo a revista americana "People", a música teria o nome de “My Place in History” ("Meu Lugar na História).

Em 2022, Parton também brincou sobre a possibilidade de não estar viva quando a cápsula fosse aberta.

“Eles não esperavam que eu estivesse lá de jeito nenhum, e provavelmente não estarei. Talvez eu esteja, quem sabe?”, afirmou.

Dolly Parton, considerada a rainha do country, morre aos 80 anos — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Dolly Parton morreu na última terça-feira (25), aos 80 anos . Cantora e compositora de sucesso, ela transcendeu o universo musical e virou um ícone pop.

Dolly enfrentava problemas de saúde desde a morte de seu marido, Carl Dean, em março de 2025. Ela cancelou uma residência de shows em maio deste ano. Segundo assessores, ela passava por tratamento contra um câncer.

Conhecida pela voz marcante, pelas perucas loiras e por seus figurinos extravagantes, Dolly construiu um império no entretenimento a partir de suas origens humildes no estado americano do Tennessee.

Com mais de 3 mil músicas em seu catálogo, a artista se consolidou como um ícone da cultura pop e expandiu sua atuação para além da música country, transitando pelo pop, bluegrass e pela era disco.

Parcerias pop e o abraço da nova geração

Mesmo sendo conhecida pelo êxito no country, Dolly sempre esteve próxima da música pop e se mostrava aberta para parcerias com novos artistas, que também celebraram sua obra.

Um dos grandes clássicos de Dolly Parton é "Jolene", hit que já foi interpretado por nomes como The White Stripes, Olivia Newton-John e Miley Cyrus.

Em 2024, a faixa ganhou uma releitura de Beyoncé no álbum "Act II: Cowboy Carter".

Em outros momentos, a artista se apresentou com nomes como Kelly Clarkson e Katy Perry. No álbum "Rockstar" (2023), ela cantou ao lado de P!nk, Lizzo e Miley Cyrus.

Amiga de longa data do também astro country e pai de Miley, Billy Ray Cyrus, a cantora assumiu o papel de madrinha de Miley desde o nascimento.

E ela levou a função a sério, tanto na vida pessoal quanto na televisão, fazendo participações na série "Hannah Montana" como Tia Dolly.

Dolly Parton na 58ª edição da Academy of Country Music Awards, em maio de 2023 — Foto: REUTERS/Mario Anzuoni

Ela foi uma das primeiras estrelas de seu nicho a abraçar abertamente a comunidade LGBTQ+.

Dolly defendeu ativamente o casamento igualitário e os direitos da comunidade muito antes que isso fosse uma pauta de destaque nos Estados Unidos.

"Se você é gay, você é gay. Se você é hétero, você é hétero. E você deveria ser quem você é e como você é."

articles.title: Estádio Rei Pelé: PGE identifica risco de colapso e pede interdição | G1
articles.standfirst: Laudo sobre as condições da estrutura é de junho de 2026. Recomendações foram encaminhadas a Selaj, que ficou de se manifestar sobre o caso por nota.
articles.summary: Laudo sobre as condições da estrutura é de junho de 2026. Recomendações foram encaminhadas a Selaj, que ficou de se manifestar sobre o caso por nota.
articles.body:
Estádio Rei Pelé, o Trapichão, em Maceió — Foto: Divulgação/Selaj

A Procuradoria-Geral do Estado de Alagoas (PGE-AL) identificou risco de colapso nas lajes superiores das rampas 2 e 3 do Estádio Rei Pelé, o “Trapichão” , em Maceió . A informação foi publicada no Diário Oficial do Estado (DOE) desta quarta-feira (26).

De acordo com o órgão, um laudo final sobre as condições da estrutura foi elaborado em junho deste ano pelo Consórcio High Tech-Progetto.

O documento foi encaminhado à Secretaria de Estado do Esporte, Lazer e Juventude de Alagoas (Selaj), responsável pelo Estádio Rei Pelé, com a recomendação de interdição parcial das rampas 2 e 3.

Segundo a 1ª Promotoria de Justiça da Capital, além da interdição, a secretaria deve adotar as seguintes medidas:

Escorar provisoriamente a estrutura das lajes;

Desocupar e interditar os alojamentos 29, 31 e 36 do Setor 5 do estádio;

Adotar as providências técnicas consideradas indispensáveis para garantir a segurança dos usuários do Rei Pelé.

O g1 procurou a Selaj, que informou que se manifestaria sobre o assunto por meio de nota. Até a publicação desta reportagem, no entanto, o documento não havia sido enviado.

A PGE também apontou outras intervenções consideradas relevantes, como a realização de correções urgentes no Setor 4 do estádio, além da recuperação e do reforço da laje da “ferradura”, no Setor 2.

A Procuradoria informou que cabe à Secretaria de Estado da Infraestrutura (Seinfra) avaliar tecnicamente essas situações, além de definir as medidas preventivas e corretivas.

Segundo o órgão, laudos anteriores não podem ser utilizados como base para avaliar os problemas identificados pelo estudo mais recente.

Por fim, a PGE recomendou que, enquanto não houver uma manifestação conclusiva que ateste a execução das medidas emergenciais e indique condições seguras para a utilização dos espaços, a Selaj impeça o acesso e o uso das áreas interditadas por qualquer pessoa.

articles.summary: O show da banda pop rock norte-americana Maroon 5 terá uma passarela de 27 metros de comprimento para aproximar os músicos dos fãs em São José do Rio Preto (SP).
articles.body:
Maroon 5 se apresentará em São José do Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: Divulgação

O show da banda pop rock norte-americana Maroon 5 terá uma passarela de 27 metros de comprimento para aproximar os músicos dos fãs em São José do Rio Preto (SP). A apresentação, inédita na cidade, será em 6 de setembro e marca abertura da turnê "Love Is Like" no Brasil.

Conforme a organização do evento, o palco será montado no Recinto de Exposições Alberto Bertelli Lucatto e terá 50 metros de largura, 18 metros de altura e 20 metros de profundidade, além da passarela que permitirá maior flexibilidade aos artistas.

A estrutura terá um “paredão” de LED de 28x12 metros e mais de 600 aparelhos de iluminação com tecnologia de ponta. Com sucessos como “Sugar”, "Moves Like Jagger" e “Maps”, a banda promete animar o público.

Esse será o segundo show internacional realizado na cidade em 2026. Em abril, a banda Guns N’ Roses se apresentou em São José do Rio Preto. Na ocasião, a atração movimentou R$ 17,4 milhões na economia local, conforme divulgado pela prefeitura.

Por meio da modalidade ingresso solidário, o público poderá adquirir os ingressos com 60% de desconto mediante a doação de 1 kg de alimento não perecível. As doações serão destinadas ao Fundo Social de Solidariedade. Os ingressos solidários podem ser adquiridos por meio do site oficial de vendas do evento.

A iniciativa está disponível para os setores Pista e Pista Premium, e o desconto será sobre o valor do ingresso inteiro. A finalidade é que os fãs vivam uma experiência inesquecível com seus ídolos e ainda pratiquem um gesto de solidariedade.
